item.title: Eagles insider teases major changes could happen by Week 10 bye
item.description: Eagles insider teases major changes could happen by Week 10 bye originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Philadelphia Eagles are 2-6 following a tough Sunday Night Football loss to the Washington Commanders in Week 8. They now sit in last place in the NFC East and currently have the No. 5 pick in the 2027 NFL Draft. With all of the issues with the team right now, including Jalen Hurts' season-ending blood clot issue and Lane Johnson's retirement, the Eagles' season is effectively over. That means a lot of change could be coming for the Eagles in the very near future. NBC Sports Philadelphia insider Ryan Fowler shared a very interesting update from an NFL source that teased the Eagles could have some major changes made by their Week 10 bye. Eagles might make major changes by Week 10 bye. "Text from a league source: 'This [Eagles] team is going to look very different come the bye... it's a loss that loses people their jobs,'" Fowler shared. "'They just got their a** kicked back to back weeks in primetime, there will be changes.'" This Eagles' team is looking very likely to undergo some changes over the next week and a half. With the NFL trade deadline eight days away, and the Eagles sitting at 2-6, they could act as major sellers. Moro Ojomo, Tariq Woolen, Dallas Goedert, Zach Baun, Hollywood Brown, Nolan Smith Jr., and a few others might be readily available for trade, and Howie Roseman is not likely to sit still at the deadline. The Eagles' Week 10 bye is a good point to make some major changes to the team, with their bye coming the same week as the trade deadline, and more than halfway through the regular season. MORE : Jayden Daniels snaps unbelievable drought with Commanders' win over Eagles Coaching changes could happen by then, and the big one is whether Nick Sirianni lasts through the deadline or not. If his Eagles team loses to the New York Giants in Week 9 after losing to the Commanders and Dallas Cowboys the previous two weeks, he might lose his job. Sean Mannion might not remain the play caller for long either, as his offense has severely underperformed, even with Tanner McKee in there with a lot of other backups. While the changes to the team aren't yet known, and there is still a chance they don't make such major changes, Eagles fans should keep a very close eye on any rumors coming out this next week, as their favorite team might look very different after the bye week. And if you're a sports fan, you may know a few names appearing on ballots. Four sports figures are among those running for Congress this year, including a former NFL kicker, former NFL sideline reporter, former New York Yankees slugger and former NFL punter. item.description: Oct 31, 2026; University Park, Pennsylvania, USA; Penn State Nittany Lions defensive end Yvan Kemajou (19) sacks Purdue Boilermakers quarterback Ryan Browne (15) during the fourth quarter of the game at West Shore Home Field at Beaver Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Matthew O'Haren-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Quarterback *Starters in Bold Ryan Browne : Snaps – 46 – Comp – 10/29 – Yds – 142 – Td – 1 – Int – 2 – Rushes – 3 – Yds – 7 Grade : F Gross. That was Ryan Browne’s worst game of the season by a wide margin. That looked more like the quarterback predicted to be the Big 10’s worst, not the one who looked like one of the biggest roster values in the nation earlier in the season. Purdue needs him to be a playmaker for this offense to work. When teams blitz, he needs to punish them, not encourage them. Browne may as well have worn a “please don’t blitz me” sign around his neck in this one because when Penn State brought the heat, he melted. According to PFF, Penn State blitzed him on 14 of his 29 passing attempts. Those 14 attempts yielded Purdue 2 completions for 9 yards and an interception. On the 15 attempts he wasn’t blitzed, he completed 8 passes for 133 yards, a touchdown, and a late game “throw it up and see what happens” interception. Part of the problem is that the running game is completely busted. Browne has played his best when the opposing defense had to worry about getting gashed by Purdue run game. When teams don’t have to worry about the run game, they can get more creative in their coverages and blitz schemes. That’s given Browne fits. He’s not seeing the blitzes, and he’s not identifying his hot routes. He’s trying to process everything after the snap and keeps running out of time. In theory, Purdue should have a couple of quality blitz-beating receivers in Townsend and Waseem who can beat press coverage early and turn short passes into long gains in man coverage. That can’t happen if Browne is surprised by the blitz on half his dropbacks. Part of playing quarterback is identifying the blitz and adjusting both the protection and receiver routes accordingly, before the snap. Quarterbacks need to do most of their thinking before the snap and react to what they see in the scant seconds before the pressure gets home. On Saturday, I saw a quarterback who was thinking with the ball in his hand instead of reacting. That’s the sign of a bad quarterback, or at least a quarterback who doesn’t have a solid understanding of what the defense is trying to do and the most efficient way to beat it. Defensive coordinators have plenty of tape on the offense now. If you can stop Purdue’s run game and make the offense one-dimensional, Ryan Browne will struggle to win the game with his arm. It’s up to Browne and offensive coordinator Josh Henson to adjust to the defensive adjustments. I haven’t seen that in the last two games. item.title: Angel Reese drops a heartwarming message for her mother after viral on-court moment
item.description: Photo by Heather Diehl/Getty Images Two days following the Atlanta Dream’s loss in Game 7 of the WNBA Finals, Angel Reese has dropped a message to express gratitude to her mother. The 24-year-old was seen walking off the court with her mother by her side following the Dream’s loss at Ballhalla. It was her first-ever trip to the WNBA Finals, and despite all the criticism Reese received, she put in a great effort, averaging 14.7 points and 12.9 rebounds. She set a record for the most rebounds ever grabbed in the WNBA Finals with her exploits against the Valkyries. Reese was visibly emotional after losing Game 7 and made a huge statement about returning to the WNBA Finals soon. She continued sending out messages to the fans and her teammates, with a special post also for her mother. “Mom, I’m so grateful I got to experience this moment with you. Every high, every low, every emotion, you’ve been right here. I love you more than words could ever explain,” wrote Reese in the caption of a picture that shows her walking off the court with her mother as the celebrations had started in Ballhalla. Her mother, Angel Webber Reese, is a former professional basketball player who also played overseas. She was the one who motivated the Dream player to play the sport, and look how that has worked out for the ‘Bayou Barbie.’ “I used to go to my mom’s games when I was younger,” she told Just Women’s Sports. “She used to play in a little league, and I used to always go watch her games on Sundays. That was something that was always inspiring to me.” She also posted a message for the fans who supported her throughout the season with a picture of her smiling in the first slide. That was followed by a picture of the 2026 Dream roster. Reese has definitely proven herself to be an elite player this season. If she can further elevate her game, the Dream can once again make a push for the WNBA title, as they have enough resources to win a championship. item.title: Cincinnati Reds claim pitchers Duncan Davitt, Paxton Schultz off waivers
item.description: WASHINGTON, DC - JULY 29: Paxton Schultz #75 of the Washington Nationals pitches during the game between the Toronto Blue Jays and the Washington Nationals at Nationals Park on Wednesday, July 29, 2026 in Washington, District of Columbia. (Photo by Alyssa McDaniel/MLB Photos via Getty Images) | MLB Photos via Getty Images Monday is a big one in terms of administrative deadlines as teams close the books on the 2026 season and look towards 2027. Chief among them is the need for players who finished the 2026 season on the 60-day IL to be returned to the 40-man roster, and that creates quite the roster crunch for some franchises. Some, though, are positioned well to take advantage of that, and the Cincinnati Reds are one. They entered the day with only 35 players on their 40-man, whereas a team like the San Francisco Giants was in need of dumping 9 players in order to scale their way down to 40. So, it’s unsurprising that the Reds jumped at the chance at a free fringe player when the option arose, and that’s precisely what happened between them and RHP Duncan Davitt. Cincinnati claimed Davitt, 27, as well as RHP Paxton Schultz from the Washington Nationals on Monday, the team announced. The #Reds today claimed off waivers RHP Duncan Davitt from the Giants and RHP Paxton Schultz from the Nationals. — Cincinnati Reds (@Reds) November 2, 2026 Both pitchers made appearances at the big league level during the 2026 regular season, yet both were viewed as fringe and/or depth arms within their two previous systems. Both also have options remaining, which is key as the Reds are going to need to craft a bullpen in 2027 capable of cycling through arms when needed given just how many holes they have in that corner of player development. Davitt was originally an 18th round pick by the Tampa Bay Rays out of the University of Iowa, and he’s spent time in with each of the Chicago White Sox, Atlanta Braves, and Giants already in his career. He’s got ample experience as both a starter and reliever and at least can boast a career K/9 of 9.4 at the minor league level even though he only has 8.0 IP in his career at the big league level. Schultz, meanwhile, is a former 14th round pick out of Utah Valley University by the Milwaukee Brewers, who was dealt to the Toronto Blue Jays in 2021. He spent five years in Toronto’s system prior to being claimed off waivers by the Nationals last January, though he does have considerably more experience at the big league level (57.0 IP) than Davitt. Both arms will fall firmly in the ‘Chase Petty, Zach McCambley, Connor Phillips’ realm of ‘throw something at the wall and hope it sticks’ corner of the Cincinnati bullpen mix, which does have some value. It also wouldn’t be a shock to hear that one, or both, is claimed by another team later in the offseason as the Reds look to use their final 40-man roster spots on more established pieces. For now, though, they both look like savvy, no-cost additions.

item.description: (Photo by Jordan Bank/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers are 6-2 heading into the bye week and are in sole possession of first place in the AFC North after their 27-6 win over the Cleveland Browns on Sunday. By the time the Steelers play their next game, the NFL trade deadline will have passed, and the Steelers are in the market for a big-name receiver. NFL insider Jason La Canfora has linked the Steelers to Jets wide receiver Garrett Wilson at the deadline. La Canfora wrote “Stay tuned,” on his X account in response to Dave Dameshek, who was reacting to the report that the Steelers are interested in the star wideout. Stay tuned https://t.co/xX8jPjFwhB — Jason La Canfora (@JasonLaCanfora) November 2, 2026 However, trading for Wilson wouldn’t be cheap for the Steelers. First off, it’s entirely possible that the rebuilding Jets would like to hold onto their young receiver to give their next quarterback a solid offensive foundation to work with. A package for Wilson would almost certainly require at least one first-round pick going to the Jets. item.description: Mandatory Credit: Kelley L Cox-Imagn Images | Kelley L Cox-Imagn Images The San Francisco 49ers haven’t needed to do anything regarding Brandon Aiyuk since they placed him on the Left Squad list in December 2025. That transaction immediately removed Aiyuk from the 53-man roster, and the team no longer has to pay him. Aiyuk’s contract was tolled, or paused. To return to the league, Aiyuk must formally apply for reinstatement. Per Over the Cap, a “ forfeitable breach ” of contract allowed the 49ers to recover portions of previously paid signing or option bonuses. According to multiple national reporters, Aiyuk is ready to return to the NFL — or at least attempt to. ESPN’s Adam Schefter tweeted that Aiyuk hired Drew Rosenhaus for representation. Rosenhaus said he is “working on getting him back to work and playing again in the NFL.” The 49ers don’t have to do anything. After Aiyuk spent the past offseason in a parasocial relationship with the Washington Commanders, he might not want to go to a team whose season is all but over. After those social media antics, it’d be surprising to see a team offer Aiyuk anything more than a minimum contract. But it’s the NFL, and the Chiefs prove every month that they don’t care what kind of person they sign. So Aiyuk likely ends up in Kansas City if he’s granted his wish to be released. A wide receiver-needy team may be willing to part ways with a late conditional pick ahead of the trade deadline. The odds feel close to a long shot that we see Aiyuk on a football field again in 2026.

item.title: Alabama football identity to be validated, or not, at LSU | Goodbread
item.description: A month ago, moments after Alabama football dispatched Mississippi State 56-23 on the road in what has arguably been the Crimson Tide's most thorough and complete victory to date, head coach Kalen DeBoer made the declaration. "The physicality up front, our guys are taking a lot of pride on both sides of the ball with what that looks like. It's become, I think, an identity … well, I know it's become an identity for us," he said. The conviction in that statement was real, and with the Crimson Tide 5-0 at the time, there was cause for it. But as Alabama (6-2, 3-2 SEC) continues preparation for a road trip at LSU on Saturday (2:30 p.m. CT, ABC), it's fair to wonder if it was also a bit premature. Because Alabama hasn't done much to prove it since. In fact, the Mississippi State game happens to be the last time the Crimson Tide outrushed an opponent. Not coincidentally, it's lost two of three games since DeBoer's comment, putting qualification for the College Football Playoff in some jeopardy. If we're being honest about what was meant by the exact phrase DeBoer used − physicality up front − it's about running the ball on one side and stopping the run on the other. It's about winning the grind required to keep your own quarterback out of third-and-longs, while placing the opposing quarterback in as many third-and-longs as possible. Not that pass protection and pass rush don't require physicality − they do − but that aspect of line play involves a little more technique from players, and is a bit more of a chess match between coordinators. The run game is more about brute power. And when an advantage of power is imposed, technique can go out the window. DeBoer's timing for the remark was noteworthy. Alabama was 5-0 at the time, but hadn't yet entered the midseason stretch that was clearly the toughest segment of the schedule. And what's made it the toughest segment, mainly, has been the opposing defenses. In three games since UA beat MSU, Georgia outrushed Alabama 206-161, Tennessee's edge was 150-54, and Texas A&M's was 115-68. That's a combined difference of 471-283, and it's a trend that can't continue if the Crimson Tide is to upset LSU (the Tigers are currently a 5.5-point favorite). item.description: Gianni Infantino has been Fifa president since 2016 [Getty Images] Fifa says "key documents" relating to president Gianni Infantino's failed plan to sell off stakes in the World Cup to private investors will be made available to members of its council. Last month, Uefa gave football's world governing body until 2 November to release details about the hugely controversial Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal, and to answer a list of questions relating to its governance and decision-making. That followed a council meeting at which Infantino apologised for the abandoned sell-off plot but failed to offer a full explanation for how the proposal was devised, asking that questions be submitted in writing. Just hours before the deadline from European football's governing body passed, Fifa secretary general Mattias Grafstrom wrote to members of its main decision-making body - saying they will be able to view "key documents", but only in person at the organisation's headquarters in Zurich. In his letter - seen by BBC Sport - he says the paperwork will be available "under strict review protocols to preserve confidentiality", with council members asked to register to see them within the next two weeks. It is unclear which documents will be made available. BBC Sport has been told Fifa viewed Uefa's two-week deadline to respond to more than 100 questions as unfeasible, given their recent focus on organising a new youth World Cup in Azerbaijan and preparations for an extraordinary congress later this month. Sources have also indicated Fifa's ability to answer some questions is limited by legal action that Uefa launched in October in the US, requesting disclosure of evidence and documents, warning it could lodge a criminal complaint in Switzerland. Last month, Uefa told Fifa that it had failed to address "a number of fundamental questions". The letter included eight pages of questions covering a number of issues, from FFE and funding to national associations, to the awarding of an inaugural Fifa Peace Prize to US President Donald Trump and the controversial suspended ban given to USA striker Folarin Balogun at the World Cup. "The withdrawal of FFE, the acknowledgement of mistakes and the announcement of 'potential governance reforms' do not answer how the relevant decisions were taken or why the Fifa Council was not involved at the appropriate stage," the letter said. "These questions require answers now. item.title: Schmidt still proving 'very bad at retiring'
item.description: Joe Schmidt was Ireland coach between 2013 and 2019 [Getty Images] "I'm not sure how good a coach I am, but I know I'm very bad at retiring from coaching." When last officially involved in Irish rugby, Joe Schmidt was apparently bringing the curtain down on one of the great coaching careers in ill-fitting fashion at the 2019 World Cup. The decision to, in his own words, "finish coaching" had been flagged a year prior. For a man who had legitimately changed the way Ireland were perceived in the rugby world, a 46-14 defeat by his native New Zealand in the quarter-finals felt no way to say goodbye to the game. As it turned out, of course, it was no such thing. Some seven years into "retirement", and the 61-year-old has since held roles with World Rugby, the All Blacks, Australia and, now, Ulster Rugby. What keeps him coming back? "I think anywhere that I have been, I've been involved with really good young men who are trying to improve what they deliver," he said. "I'm just a schoolteacher, and I'm just still trying to teach people as best I can. "That's irrespective of where I am at any particular time." 'Small steps' for Schmidt at Ulster - Best 'I played with his voice in my head' - Schmidt's influence on Ireland Schmidt has an amazing eye for detail - Dermody After serving as a selector with New Zealand and head coach of the Wallabies, Schmidt describes his current role with Ulster as one that is "more for the future than the present", with an official title of coach development advisor. The "pretty flexible" arrangement in Belfast will see him spend this month offering support and guidance to coaches through all levels of the province's pathways before returning again in April for another stint. In between, there will be remote work. With stories of his rugby obsession well-worn, it will surprise few that such study has already started in earnest, even during his downtime last week while working with Australia A in America. Despite enjoying such successes with Leinster before taking the Ireland job in 2013, with one of his two Heineken Cup successes coming thanks to a thumping final victory over Ulster, he does not feel strange now being associated with a different province. "It's funny, I'm just coaching, so it's often not about the tracksuit top [you're wearing]," he said. "It's just about trying to do a good job, trying to develop understanding, improve technique, and that doesn't really change. I don't think I change. "But it's doesn't feel foreign. I've spent plenty of time in this stadium. In fact, before this stadium was built [in 2014], I spent a fair bit of time in an old wooden one that was here. It's not something I'm uncomfortable with." Indeed, it was in part those pre-existing relationships at what is now the Affidea Stadium that helped pave his way for the surprising switch. item.title: Patriots unlikely to face Packers’ Micah Parsons even with practice return looming
item.description: The Green Bay Packers are getting some reinforcement ahead of their upcoming game with the New England Patriots. Micah Parsons, the four-time All-Pro edge rusher, is set to return to practice this week. Packers head coach Matt LaFleur announced the news on Monday. “That would be the intention,” he said during a press conference. “It’s going to be a process trying to get him back. We’re hopeful. It’s going to be dependent on the next couple of days, but we’re hopeful it’s going to be sometime this week.” Parsons, 27, started the regular season on the physically unable to perform list after tearing his ACL last December. When he went down, the Packers’ high-profile trade acquisition via the Dallas Cowboys had 12.5 sacks and a pair of forced fumbles on his 2025 résumé. While Parsons returning to practice opens the window for his return to Green Bay’s active roster and would make him eligible to play in Sunday’s contest in Foxborough, an immediate return to game action is not a guarantee. Last week, Rob Demovsky of ESPN noted that “[e]ven if Parsons practices next week, it would be highly unlikely he could play in the Week 9 game at the Patriots.” According to a report by NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport, Nov. 25 against the Los Angeles Rams is Parsons’ targeted return date. LeFleur hinted at that approach as well on Monday. “Like everything around here, it’s pretty fluid in terms of how he responds and just the progress he’s going to, hopefully, continue to make leading up to when he’s available,” he said. “If I had a bet on it, it’s going to be more toward the longer end than the shorter end.” For the Patriots, facing a Parsons-less Packers team is the preferred scenario. Even if not at a 100%, he has the ability to make game-changing plays against an offensive line that has had to deal with its fair share of injury questions this season. The Patriots have lost both of their starting guards to injury, while both of their tackles also got banged up at one point. Heading into Sunday’s game, New England’s projected O-line will feature Will Campbell and Morgan Moses at tackle, with two of Ben Brown, Matt Pryor and Walter Rouse flanking center Jared Wilson at the guard positions. Kickoff between the two storied franchise is scheduled for 4:25 p.m. ET on Sunday, Nov. 8.

The San Francisco 49ers could really use some wide receiver help this season. As they come out of their Week 8 bye, the team is dealing with injuries to Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel, and plenty of their other top WR options. But one player who is not playing but is healthy, and surely would've been a big help right about now, is Brandon Aiyuk. He hasn't made any effort to come back to the NFL, but according to NFL insider Jordan Schultz , Aiyuk was closing in on a new agent hire. There isn't anything the 49ers need to do. But the moment he does file for reinstatement, the 49ers will then be put on the clock to make a decision about his contract and how best to go forward.
